description:
FILED s523b (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-20) from #3672's measurement.  PRE-EXISTING (base 6cf75804).  A tied scalar whose FETCH returns a REFERENCE, passed to a sub, is FETCHed twice where perl fetches once (and a `($)` sub returning `$_[0]` in void context fetches twice where perl fetches 0 times).  A string-valued tied scalar is right.
PROBE scratch/s523b/p4/gm6.pl (perl / base / tree):
  sub two { my $x = $_[0]; $x }   two($v)    perl 1   PCL 2
  sub one ($) { $_[0] }           one($v)    perl 0   PCL 2
  sub none { 1 }                  none($v)   perl 0   PCL 0
  (string FETCH)                  two($w)    perl 1   PCL 1
  my $y = $v                                 perl 1   PCL 1
So the extra read is in the `$_[0]` read / call-return path when the fetched value is a reference (a ref test before the copy?).  Measure where: count FETCH around `my $x = $_[0]` alone vs the call.  Rows: none blessed today (getmagic-once.t passes 6/0 after #3672); perl-tests op/tie_fetch_count.t is the population.
subject: A tied scalar whose FETCH returns a REFERENCE, passed to a sub, is FETCHed twice (perl once; a ($) sub returning $_[0] in void: perl 0)
